classification.difficultyReason: Connect the projection formula with the geometric dot product, then use the supplied part-a result and Pythagoras to derive the rejection magnitude; both proof methods are explicitly signposted.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Given nonzero vectors $\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b}$ with acute angle $\theta$ between them and $|\underset{\sim}{a}|=r$, prove, using the vector projection and dot product formulas, that the magnitude of the component of vector $\underset{\sim}{a}$ parallel to $\underset{\sim}{b}$, $|\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}|$, is $r\cos\theta$.

spec.description: Acute projection triangle with black original vector, blue parallel component, dashed red perpendicular and dashed blue supporting-line extension. Coordinates define illustrative shape only; no numerical dimensions are asserted.
spec.mathematics: OP is the orthogonal projection of OA, with AP perpendicular to OP; |OA|=r and angle POA=theta.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied geometry and labels remain visible in the question edition.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}&=\frac{\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}}{|\underset{\sim}{b}|^2}\underset{\sim}{b}\\ |\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}|&=\left|\frac{\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}}{|\underset{\sim}{b}|^2}\right|\,|\underset{\sim}{b}|\\ |\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}|&=\frac{|\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}|}{|\underset{\sim}{b}|}\end{aligned}$$

Using $\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=|\underset{\sim}{a}|\,|\underset{\sim}{b}|\cos\theta$ and $\cos\theta>0$ for the acute angle $\theta$:

$$\begin{aligned}|\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}|&=\frac{|\underset{\sim}{a}|\,|\underset{\sim}{b}|\cos\theta}{|\underset{\sim}{b}|}\\ |\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}|&=|\underset{\sim}{a}|\cos\theta\\ |\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}|&=r\cos\theta.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Prove, using the result in part a and Pythagoras’ theorem, that the rejection magnitude $|\underset{\sim}{a}-\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}|$ is $r\sin\theta$.

spec.description: Same triangle as part a, with the perpendicular rejection shown as a red arrow directed from the projection foot towards the tip of the original vector.
spec.mathematics: OA=OP+PA, OP perpendicular to PA; the rejection is PA.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied geometry and labels remain visible in the question edition.

answer.worked:
The projection and rejection are perpendicular. By Pythagoras’ theorem and part a:

$$\begin{aligned}|\underset{\sim}{a}-\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}|^2&=|\underset{\sim}{a}|^2-|\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}|^2\\ |\underset{\sim}{a}-\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}|^2&=r^2-r^2\cos^2\theta\\ |\underset{\sim}{a}-\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}|^2&=r^2(1-\cos^2\theta)\\ |\underset{\sim}{a}-\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}|^2&=r^2\sin^2\theta.\end{aligned}$$

Since $r>0$ and $\sin\theta>0$,

$$\therefore\quad |\underset{\sim}{a}-\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}|=r\sin\theta.$$
